subject: Checkout embedding latency spike — orchestration & temporary fallback options
messages:
From: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@argoretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Checkout embedding latency spike — customers seeing >350ms p95 increase

Marcus / Marissa,

Over the last 2 hours we're seeing a sharp increase in checkout latency that lines up with calls to your embedding endpoint used during cart validation. p95 for the embedding-lookup step has jumped ~350ms, and our conversion funnel for the checkout widget is down ~2.8% vs baseline. We attach a small sample of logs and a perf trace (argoretail-logs-20270821.zip).

Can Redwood confirm:
- is there an ongoing rollout or config change on embedding model variants or cache TTLs?
- any recommended immediate mitigations (pin older model, increase instance buffer, or temporary traffic-shaping)?

We're pushing a quick feature-flag to reduce calls on our side, but we need your advice on whether we should expect this to persist or if you can apply a short-term fix so we can re-enable the higher-traffic experience.

Thanks — this is impacting a small but revenue-sensitive merchant cohort. Happy to take a call now if useful.

— Rahul
Rahul Singh
Head of Platform Engineering, Argo Retail
rahul.singh@argoretail.com

Attachment: argoretail-logs-20270821.zip (log bundle, 2.3 MB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 16:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout embedding latency spike — triage plan

Looping SRE and product. Initial notes:

1) Marcus — you own customer-facing comms; recommend a short ack to Rahul that we're triaging and propose a 30-min check-in.
2) Ben / Soojin / Diego — please run these immediate checks:
   - confirm recent model variant rollouts or quantization changes to embedding serving in us-west region (last 6 hours)
   - inspect KV cache hit-rate and eviction metrics for embedding tables used by Argo Retail (keyspace argoretail-prod)
   - check autoscaler decision logs and any sudden container kill/restart events
3) Product (Grace) — need a quick decision on whether we can allow a temporary fallback to the previous model/serving profile for Argo only (can be implemented as routing rule + soft pin). If yes, we'll prepare a short rollback plan.

I'll draft an update for Rahul once we have a signal from SRE (target: 45 minutes).

— Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout embedding latency spike — preliminary findings

Quick update from triage:

- No new model deployment shows up in the rollout graph in the last 8 hours for the embedding family. Kernel and quant paths look unchanged.
- We are seeing a spike in KV cache eviction for the embedding keyspace used by Argo Retail starting ~15:40 UTC. Evictions correlate with a ~3x surge in unique user prefixes (likely a client-side cache warming pattern after a CDN purge) — hit-rate dropped from 92% to 58%.
- When hit-rate drops, per-call tokenization + embedding lookup moves from fast-path cached to full-model path and adds ~300-400ms p95 on median requests.

Short-term mitigations we can apply (safe, low-risk):
1) Increase cache size for argoretail-prod keyspace by 25% (config flip, immediate effect) — downside: marginally higher memory usage; requires SRE approval.
2) Serve Argo traffic from an older cached snapshot model variant (read-only pin at routing layer) for 2–6 hours while their cache warms. This requires a routing exception but preserves correctness.
3) Configure client-side guidance: recommend Argo throttle burstiness and keep-alive behavior while we stabilize.

I attached a short diagnostics note: cache_evap_diag.txt. My recommendation: apply (1) immediately and (2) if we don't see recovery in 30–45 minutes. Need product sign-off for (2) due to routing policy implications.

— Ben
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: cache_evap_diag.txt
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 17:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout embedding latency spike — product decision and comms draft

Grace / Marcus — product asks we need answered for the routing-exception fallback:

- Can we approve a temporary per-tenant routing pin to the last-stable embedding snapshot for Argo Retail for up to 6 hours? This would be a read-only routing rule and would not change model weights.
- If approved, do we want the pin to be manual (on-demand) or automated if hit-rate stays below 70% for >20 minutes?
- SLA/approval: we need a single approver (Grace or Marcus) to greenlight the routing exception during off-hours.

I took a pass at a customer-facing note (proposed_cust_note_v1.md) — short summary + what we're doing and an ask for a 2-hour load window reduction while caches rebuild. Excerpt below:

--- proposed customer note excerpt ---
Hi Rahul — thanks for the alert. Our SRE team has identified a temporary cache-evaporation event that is increasing downstream latency for certain embedding calls. We're applying an immediate increase to your cache quota and can pin your traffic to a last-stable snapshot as a fallback while your cache warms (no model changes). Can you accept a 2-hour reduced-traffic window for a full warm-up? We'll confirm when p95 returns to normal.
--- end excerpt ---

If product approves the pin, SRE will implement (routing change + cache bump) and we can send the note. Marcus — do you want to lead the external message or should I send the initial note?

— Soojin
Senior SRE/Incident Ops
From: Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@argoretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout embedding latency spike — orchestration & temporary fallback options

Thanks team — appreciate the quick triage and proposed mitigations. We can accept the 2-hour reduced-traffic window tomorrow (Wed) 02:00–04:00 UTC for your maintenance and pin/restore as needed. Please proceed with the cache bump and routing pin approach; confirm when the routing exception is in place and I'll re-enable the higher-traffic checkout flag on our side.

If you prefer, we can do a short call to coordinate; otherwise, we'll stand by.

— Rahul
